<!--
numbered-lines puts a number beside every line, which APA asks for on a
manuscript sent out for review. It worked in .docx and in apaquarto-pdf, which
draws them with lineno, and in neither apaquarto-latex-pdf nor apaquarto-typst.

apa7 leaves lineno's own look alone: a number half the size of the body, right
aligned, ten points clear of the text block, five in journal mode where the
text is smaller and a column has less room beside it. Both formats match those
three now, measured against apa7 in each of its four modes.

Numbering lines is not offered in .html, where there are no pages and no line
boxes a stylesheet can count.
-->

# Method

The first paragraph of the body, written long enough to wrap over more than
one line so that the line numbers have something to number, with more words
after them to be sure of it in every mode.

A second paragraph, also long enough to wrap, so that the count carries on past
the first one and can be seen to do so.
